name: Origami Fold
summary: A world folded from washi paper: flat facets with crisp mountain and valley creases on a giant crease-pattern sheet.
description: Every character, creature, prop, collectible and icon is a small fold mesh: flat triangular facets whose tone comes from one light in the upper left, picked from a 4-step ramp per paper colour. Shared edges are classified automatically into mountain folds (a thin bright line) and valley folds (a thin dark line), and the paper is two-sided, so hems, inner ears, bellies and wing backs show the cream back of the sheet. The ground is one huge sheet scored with a crease tessellation, with pastel sheets laid on top along straight folded hems and pleated blue water sunk below. Soft sheared drop shadows lift every folded object off the paper.
avoidFor: projects that need hundreds of distinct animated models

difficulty.why: Each new asset is a list of triangles with a pseudo height per vertex – shading and every crease line follow automatically, so a new creature is mostly composing kites, strips and fans. The craft is in choosing folds that read as real origami and keeping silhouettes simple; animation means rebuilding the mesh per frame and baking it (both facing directions are baked separately so the light stays upper-left).

technique.renderer: Canvas 2D (procedural, no image assets): 2D fold meshes with pseudo heights -> per-facet flat tone -> automatic crease classification -> baked sprites
technique.resolution: Native resolution. Sprites are baked at K = clamp(round(screenHeight/360 * 1.6), 3, 8) px per world unit (4 px/unit at 900 px); the ground is baked in 256-unit chunks at up to 2.5 px/unit (groundResMax 2.5).
technique.summary: Shapes are triangle lists in screen space with a z height per vertex; the facet normal against one light picks 1 of 4 tones, and each shared edge is drawn as a mountain (bright) or valley (dark) crease depending on the fold direction. Meshes are baked once into sprites, mirrored copies are rebuilt (not flipped) so light stays upper-left.
technique.linework: No ink outline. Open paper edges are stroked in the ramp's deep tone mixed 38 % toward ink #2a2433 at 0.55 units; mountain folds 0.3 units in the light tone mixed 55 % with white at alpha 0.9; valley folds 0.3 units in the deep tone at alpha 0.6; seams between two paper colours at alpha 0.45. Round joins and caps. Each facet is also stroked in its own fill colour (0.9 px) to hide anti-aliasing seams.
technique.shading: Flat per facet. d = n·L with L = normalize(-0.55, -0.45, 0.7) (x right, y down the screen, z towards the viewer); tone = d > 0.8 light, > 0.55 base, > 0.3 shade, else deep. A flat facet is the base tone; far legs and far wings add +1 tone for depth. No gradients inside a facet.
technique.lighting: One soft light from the upper left for everything (models, ground relief, water pleats). Cast shadows are the sprite silhouette tinted rgb(78,56,72), sheared to the lower right (x' = x - 0.62*y, y' = -0.36*y around the feet), blurred 1.1-1.6 units at alpha 0.24-0.32, plus a contact ellipse. A screen overlay adds warm light rgba(255,250,235,.16) at the upper left and plum shade rgba(90,64,80,.14) at the lower right with a soft vignette rgba(96,70,70,.17).
technique.texture: Paper fibre: a 160 px tileable canvas of 420 short curved fibres (white at alpha 0.3-0.65, brown rgba(120,92,64,0.1-0.22)) plus 900 speckles, laid over every sprite with source-atop at 0.55 and over the ground at 0.5.

paletteRules: Every paper colour is a 4-step ramp (light / base / shade / deep); the light picks the step per facet – never invent in-between colours or gradients.
The ground is pale washi (white #f4eee1 and pastel sheets); everything standing on it uses the saturated mid-value ramps, so actors pop by value and hue.
Kami paper is two-sided: wherever a sheet turns over (hems, bellies, inner ears, wing undersides, confetti backs) use the cream ramp.

Main character = coral + indigo + cream + dark paws; small creatures = teal / sage / mustard; fast creature = blush; large creature = plum with a mustard mane – keep creature hues off the main character.
Water is the only large saturated ground area (#88a8d8) and always sits below the paper with an inner shadow.
Shadows are plum rgb(78,56,72) at low alpha, never black or grey; no pure black anywhere (darkest is #201c27).

world.summary: One endless sheet of washi paper scored with a crease tessellation (40-unit squares with both diagonals). Pastel sheets lie on top of it, their outlines following the crease lines so every border is a straight folded edge with a cream hem and an offset drop shadow; water is a blue pleated sheet sunk below the paper. Major folds every 160 units are marked in origami diagram notation.
layers: Crease tessellation: 40-unit squares, each split into 4 triangles (N, E, S, W) by its diagonals; one region id per triangle from fbm noise (water: fbm(x/720) > 0.64 away from the centre; sheets: fbm(x/420) >= 0.5, colour from fbm(x/1000) -> sage / mustard / coral / teal)

Relief: every 160-unit panel has its own pattern (42 % pyramids, 26 % waterbomb checker, 16 % horizontal pleats, 16 % twist); a triangle's colour is multiplied by 1 + relief*amp, relief N +0.022, E -0.017, S -0.027, W +0.013, amp 0.35-1.25 from noise

Layers drawn bottom to top: water, base sheet, sage, mustard, coral, teal; before each layer its union is filled twice offset (+1.3,+1.6) alpha 0.09 and (+2.6,+3.2) alpha 0.07 in rgba(84,60,58) – a soft drop shadow onto the lower layers
Hems: along every edge that borders a lower layer, a 2.4-unit strip inside the sheet in its colour mixed 55 % toward #fffcf4, with a fold line rgba(96,72,60,.22) and the paper edge rgba(96,72,60,.34)

Water: chevron pleats (period 18, row 11, amplitude 3.4) – shaded slope #6d8cc6, valley line rgba(44,64,122,.32), lit slope #a9c3ea, ridge line rgba(255,255,255,.7); small cream three-facet wave crests on a 52-unit grid

Crease lines: mountain diagonals rgba(255,253,246,.7) 0.45 with a faint shadow twin offset 0.5; valley lines rgba(98,76,60,.16); grid lines rgba(98,76,60,.13); pleat panels draw alternating horizontal mountain/valley lines
Major folds every 4 cells in diagram notation: valley = dashed [5, 3.5] indigo rgba(59,74,135,.28), mountain = dash-dot [7, 2.5, 1.2, 2.5] coral rgba(201,91,71,.3)
Paper fibre over the whole chunk at alpha 0.5

Sparse flat decals on a 21-unit grid (13 % of cells): folded grass blades (sage/pine strips), 4-petal folded flowers in blush/cream/mustard, two-tone paper scraps, and rare curved fold arrows in indigo

characters.summary: Upright and creature models are small fold meshes of 10-60 facets in 3/4 side view, baked for both facing directions (mirrored geometry, re-lit). The main character (~26 x 36 units with ears and tail) is a coral origami fox: a faceted head with a raised muzzle peak, two kite ears with cream inner sides, an indigo kimono folded down the middle with a mustard sash and cream hem, dark ink paws and a big kite tail with a cream tip. Creatures: a jumping frog (small, teal / sage / mustard, cream belly), a paper crane (fast, blush, hovers 8 units up, wings show the cream back on the down-stroke) and a plum folded boar (large, ~46 x 40 units) with a mustard spiked mane, cream tusk and belly band.
rules: Build everything from kites (two triangles folded along an axis), folded strips (legs, necks, tails) and fans around one raised point (heads, bodies, crowns); the raised point sets where the light breaks.
Keep 2-3 colours per model plus the cream back side; the main character is the only coral-and-indigo figure.
Silhouette first: big ears, tails, wings and manes are the readable shapes – details are only ink dot eyes (0.75-0.85 units, white catch-light) and a dot nose.
Never flip a sprite with a negative scale: rebuild the mirrored mesh so the light stays in the upper left.

Main character: 4 walk frames + idle + dash pose, 1.1-unit step bob; frog: sit / crouch / leap frames with a 4.5-unit hop arc and tilt; crane: 4 wing frames at 10 fps; boar: 4 heavy walk frames with a 1.3-unit body bob.
Appearing: ground creatures fold up out of a flat four-facet square of their own colour (outBack on the vertical scale); the crane drops in from 30 units while fading in.
Vanishing: the creature flattens into its sheet (scale y -> 0.15, x -> 1.35, fading) while the impact burst takes over; hit flash is a cream #fffaf0 silhouette over the sprite plus a short squash.

props.summary: Folded scenery baked with the same fold engine and light: tiered pines, round trees with a geodesic folded crown, faceted boulders, the classic origami house (cream walls, coral or indigo roof with cream squash-fold flaps), tulip clusters, a spinning pinwheel, an accordion screen, and on the water paper boats and lotus flowers.
rules: Pines: three kite tiers (half-widths 15.5 / 11.7 / 7.9) folded down the middle so the left half is lit, on a wood strip trunk; pine green or teal.
Round trees: crown of 8 outer + 8 inner points and a raised apex (24 facets) in coral, mustard, sage or teal on a strip trunk with one branch.
Boulders: a fan of 7 jittered points around a raised point at the upper left, stone ramp; one variant has a second small stone.
House: front walls folded slightly at the middle, side wall one tone darker, door indigo, window mustard, roof as one folded triangle with two cream flap triangles.
Pinwheel: 12 baked rotation frames (coral and teal blades, cream inner flaps) on a stick, turning at 9 frames per second.
Paper boats and lotus sit only on water, bob 0.8 units and rock ±0.05 rad with an expanding cream ripple ellipse.
Every land prop casts the same sheared, blurred plum shadow as the characters; tall props turn 50 % translucent when the main character is behind them.

effects.name: Paper-plane projectile
effects.how: A folded dart (cream wings with coral tips, valley crease down the middle) baked at 16 angles so the light stays upper-left, with its own soft shadow 7 units below and two short pencil dashes #7a6c74 behind it.

effects.name: Orbiting shuriken
effects.how: A two-tone origami throwing star (coral and teal arms around a raised centre) baked in 8 rotation frames over 90°, spinning at 30 frames per second over a soft shadow blob.

effects.name: Collectibles
effects.how: Small: a mustard lucky star (5 points, 10 facets, 6 rotation frames). Large: a teal folded crystal (4 facets) turning through 8 frames. Both bob 3 ± 1.2 units over a plum blob shadow.

effects.name: Unfolding burst
effects.how: When a creature vanishes: 8-12 two-tone kite petals in its colour and cream shoot outward and fold shut again (length 0.5 -> 1.3 -> 0, sin envelope), its flat square sheet tumbles up and away (flipping between colour front and cream back), and 8-16 confetti triangles follow; the large creature adds a dash-dot crease ring.

effects.name: Two-sided confetti
effects.how: Flat triangles that flip with cos(t*9): the colour front (light/base tone) when positive, the cream back when negative, with a gentle sideways sway, gravity 50-120 and high drag so they flutter.

effects.name: Impact
effects.how: A crisp 4-point folded sparkle (cream with a thin plum edge) at hit height plus 3 two-tone shards (light/shade halves) with gravity 260.

effects.name: Glow-up
effects.how: A dashed mustard crease ellipse opening to 40 units, a ground-level ring of 10 mustard/coral petals plus 8 teal/cream petals, and 22 confetti triangles drifting down from 30-46 units; the main character turns once like a card (horizontal scale cos(2πt), mirrored sprite on the back half).

effects.name: Dash strips
effects.how: Thin folded paper strips (light/shade halves) in cream and indigo trail behind the dash direction, three cream afterimages of the main character fade at alpha 0.38/i.

effects.name: Floating numbers
effects.how: Zen Maru Gothic 900 in indigo #3b4a87 with a cream #fffbf3 border; emphasised values are deep coral #9b4136 on a folded mustard tag (two halves #f8d372 / #e6ae42 with a cream crease). They unfold vertically from a crease (outBack) and fold away.

atmosphere.summary: A calm, evenly lit paper table: one soft light from the upper left, sheared plum drop shadows to the lower right, layered sheets casting short offset shadows, a faint warm light gradient across the screen and a few origami butterflies drifting over the paper.
rules: One light direction for everything: L = normalize(-0.55, -0.45, 0.7); shadows always fall to the lower right.

Cast shadow = silhouette tinted rgb(78,56,72), sheared x' = x - 0.62*y, y' = -0.36*y, blurred 1.1 units (props 1.6), alpha 0.3 (crane 0.24, props 0.28) + contact ellipse; flying things get an unsheared, flattened shadow offset by their height.
Screen overlay baked once per size: linear gradient from rgba(255,250,235,.16) at the upper left to rgba(90,64,80,.14) at the lower right, plus a radial vignette to rgba(96,70,70,.17).
Ambient life: origami butterflies (two kite wings, flap by horizontal scale 0.25-1 at 11 rad/s) on a 230-unit grid, 22 ± 4 units above their shadows.
No glow, no bloom, no fog – paper is matte; brightness differences come from facets only.
Modal overlays: indigo tint linear-gradient(135deg, rgba(59,74,135,.34), rgba(40,52,98,.5)) with a diagonal crease grid of rgba(255,250,240,.13) lines every 64 px.

ui.summary: UI is folded paper: bars are cream strips folded lengthwise (top half lighter, bottom half shaded) with pleated fills, the clock is an envelope with a flap and diagonal creases, counters are paper tabs with a dog-eared corner, the caption bar is a note folded down the middle and cards are envelopes with a coloured flap triangle that unfold (rotateX from the top edge) into place. Hard offset shadows rgba(82,60,72,.15), 1 px edges rgba(120,96,80,.24), no rounded corners.

motion: Main character: 4 walk frames over 4.6 animation units per cycle with a |sin| step bob of 1.1 units; idle breathing ±1.8 % vertical; small 0.04 rad lean while walking.
Small creature: hop cycle anim*0.5 – 20 % crouch squash (8 %), 58 % airborne with a 4.5-unit arc and nose-up tilt −0.2 rad, then land.
Fast creature: 4 wing frames at 10 per second, hover 8 ± 1.8 units, banking ±0.12 rad with its velocity.
Large creature: 4 walk frames at anim*0.32*4, 1.3-unit body bob, ±0.03 rad sway.
Appear 0.45 s: flat sheet rotates 1.6 rad and shrinks while the creature unfolds upward (outBack after 25 %); vanish 0.35 s: flatten and fade.
Glow-up: one card-flip turn in the first third of a second; numbers unfold from a crease in 14 % of their life and fold away in the last 22 %.
HUD cards unfold from their top edge (perspective rotateX −88° -> 0) in 0.6 s, staggered 0.08 s; the title ribbon unfolds horizontally (scaleX 0.05 -> 1).
do: Model every asset as facets with a z height per vertex and let one shared light choose 1 of 4 tones per facet.
Draw shared edges as creases: bright for mountain folds, dark for valley folds; stroke only open edges as paper edges.
Show the cream back of the paper wherever a sheet turns over – hems, bellies, inner ears, wing backs, confetti.
Keep the ground pale and structured by its crease pattern; put colour on things standing on it.
Let region borders follow crease lines so every edge between sheets is straight, hemmed and shadowed.
Bake both facing directions from mirrored geometry so the light never flips.
Lift every folded object with a soft plum shadow falling to the lower right.
dont: Don't use smooth gradients, soft airbrush shading or rounded blobs – paper folds are straight.
Don't add thick black outlines; edges are paper edges in the colour's deep tone.
Don't mirror sprites with negative scale – the light would jump to the right.
Don't cut organic, torn or scissor-cut silhouettes – that is cut-paper, not origami.
Don't fill the ground with saturated colour or dense decals; it must stay quiet behind the actors.
Don't make shadows black or grey, and don't let them point in different directions.
Don't use glows, bloom or neon – paper is matte.
performance: All fold meshes are baked at init (main character 6 poses x 2 directions, 3 x 3 frog sprites x 2, 4 crane and 4 boar frames x 2, 19 props, 12 pinwheel frames, 16 plane angles, 8 shuriken, 6 star and 8 crystal frames, butterflies) together with their blurred shadow sprites – roughly 150-250 ms. Hit flashes are lazily tinted copies. Per frame only drawImage blits, a few particle paths and one full-screen overlay: about 1 ms of script for 100+ creatures. Ground chunks (256 units, up to 640 px) are vector-drawn by a generator yielding per layer and every 16 decals (about 4 ms each), with a region cache for the per-triangle noise; ctx.filter blur is used only at bake time.
